successCriteria.description: The "Request leave" link (a react-router-dom Link to /leaves/new) is rendered in every render state of LeaveListPage: the error state, the loading state, the empty-list state, and the populated-list state.

A unit test asserts the link is present when the list is loading (requests === null), when the list is empty, when the list is populated, and when an error is set — i.e. the link is not gated behind the final populated-list return.
The existing list rendering (loading indicator, error alert, empty message, and per-request list items) remains intact and unchanged in behavior after the link is relocated.

constraints: The link must use react-router-dom's Link component pointing to /leaves/new (the route already registered in App.tsx); do not introduce a plain anchor or a different target.
No change to LeaveListPageProps, the ILeaveService contract, or the leaveService.list() call — this phase only relocates the link within the existing component.
The link must remain reachable/visible without requiring a successful list load — it must not be nested inside the populated-list branch or any conditional that depends on requests/error state.
Keep the existing error/loading/empty/populated early-return structure's observable output (role="alert", "Loading…", "No leave requests", list items) unchanged; only the link's placement changes.
outOfScope: No changes to App.tsx routing, RequestLeavePage, LeaveDetailPage, the leave service, or the API client — the /leaves/new route and RequestLeavePage already exist from prior phases.
No changes to the list data fetching, error handling, or the LeaveRequestView rendering logic.

ambiguities.description: Whether the link should be visually styled/positioned identically across all four states (e.g. always at top) or may differ per state.
options: Always render at the top of the page in every state
Render in a consistent location but allow minor layout differences per state

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The link must target the route path /leaves/new exactly as registered in App.tsx, so navigation resolves to the RequestLeavePage route.
The link must use the same react-router-dom Link import and rendering style already used in LeaveListPage (and LeaveDetailPage) for the per-request links.
The component's public contract (LeaveListPageProps with leaveService: ILeaveService) and its export from the presentation index must remain unchanged.
